everyday-objects-02.semantic_alignment: A pronged utensil used for eating.

claims.proposition: Indonesian “garpu” and Malaysian “garpu” are both the common everyday terms for a fork, a pronged utensil used for eating.

everyday-objects-05.semantic_alignment: The edible vegetable also called aubergine.

claims.proposition: Indonesian “terong” and Malaysian “terung” are the common everyday terms for the same vegetable; the spelling differs by locale.

everyday-objects-06.semantic_alignment: The large fruit with sweet flesh and a green rind.

claims.proposition: For watermelon, Indonesian commonly uses “semangka” while Malaysian Malay commonly uses “tembikai”; these are different everyday words for the same fruit.

everyday-objects-07.semantic_alignment: An edible starchy root with sweet flesh.

claims.proposition: For sweet potato, Indonesian commonly uses “ubi jalar” while Malaysian Malay commonly uses “keledek” or “ubi keledek”; these are different everyday terms for the same root.

everyday-objects-08.semantic_alignment: Liquid detergent used to wash dishes by hand.

claims.proposition: Indonesian “sabun cuci piring” and Malaysian “cecair pencuci pinggan” refer to dishwashing detergent, but the Indonesian term can be broader than liquid specifically, while the Malaysian term explicitly denotes liquid.
